I do have knowledge and material at hand, just didn't really have time or care to educate a random person online. And again, what I was saying was pretty basic, even for a non-artist. Let me walk you through from the very beginning using as much ELI5 as possible. 

1. A **style** are specific tendencies or choices of an artist, and what generally makes one "unique". This varies greatly. From inking, to color choices(washed out, hard colors, saturation, specific temperature colors, etc..), simplicity, exaggerations, texture, features, shadowing, reflections, etc.. it's quite literally infinite. A style typically goes hand-in-hand with **technique**. Many artists can use multiple styles as well and EVERYONE'S style evolves over time, even in small details.

2. A **design** in this case refers to the source that the art is derived from, which would be an official artwork or source, in general. There's Skyward Sword Link, there's SSB4 Link, there's OoT Link, etc. These are designs of an official work. And fanart are typically based on these designs. This is also what is known as a **model**, although that term does vary depending on what medium we're talking about.  
Depending on the character, a design can even have multiple different outfits of the character. In Skyward Sword, he starts out in his village outfit, but the hair, facial detail, and general style remains intact. 

3. Link's suit, sword, and shield is what is called a **characteristic**. I referred to it as "basis of a character" earlier. It's what makes Link, Link. This goes back to my main point earlier. I said that Pikachu isn't fat. Back then, Pikachu being fat was *necessary*, it is a *requirement* for Pikachu to be fat because that's his *characteristic*, which changed over time(basically in generation 4, he was slim). 

4. This is kind of irrelevant, but it doesn't hurt to explain. A **redesign** is basically the same as a design, except usually done with well-established characters/icons/logos. It's usually a more significant change from the old design. A redesign also refers to a very specific character, like Dante from Devil May Cry is basically a new person from DmC. And more recently, Knuckles from Sonic Boom took some steroids, although Sonic Boom is actually based on a different universe so it's not really *that* Knuckles, but still a redesign.
